verdict.rationale: Omarchy documents a menu-driven way to create and run a Windows VM (Install > Windows), built on a Docker VM with hardware virtualization, a shared clipboard and a shared folder, so little manual setup is needed. That covers only one guest OS, and the user must still supply a valid Windows 11 Pro license. Missing for 10: general-purpose VM creation for Linux or other guest OSes, documented VM lifecycle management (start/stop/list), and independent hands-on corroboration that the Windows VM setup is quick and configuration-free.

support.subject: As a developer, I can quickly create and run virtual machines without manual configuration

citations.quote: Omarchy offers an easy way to run Windows through a Docker VM.
Choose _Install > Windows_ from the Omarchy menu. Hardware virtualization brings near-native CPU performance for Office and everyday work, with a shared clipboard and a folder for moving files
Bring a Windows 11 Pro license valid for a VM.
